facts.value: A systematic review evaluated 45 studies that examined the relationship between physical activity and cancer survival rates.
facts.programme_association: Exercise and Health Fitness Management - BSc

facts.value: Physical activity is associated with reduced all-cause, breast cancer–specific, and colon cancer–specific mortality according to 27 observational studies.
facts.programme_association: Exercise and Health Fitness Management - BSc

facts.value: There is currently insufficient evidence regarding the association between physical activity and mortality for survivors of other cancers.
facts.programme_association: Exercise and Health Fitness Management - BSc

facts.value: Exercise may positively affect the quality of life in cancer survivors, including factors such as anxiety, self-esteem, and emotional well-being.
facts.programme_association: Exercise and Health Fitness Management - BSc

facts.value: For people with cancer undergoing active treatment, exercise may have positive effects on health-related quality of life, such as fatigue and physical functioning.
facts.programme_association: Exercise and Health Fitness Management - BSc

facts.value: The positive effects of exercise are likely to be more pronounced with higher intensity exercise.
facts.programme_association: Exercise and Health Fitness Management - BSc

facts.value: Exercise may contribute to a reduction of cancer-related fatigue in survivors of breast cancer.
facts.programme_association: Exercise and Health Fitness Management - BSc

facts.value: People with cancer cachexia are encouraged to engage in physical exercise.
facts.programme_association: Exercise and Health Fitness Management - BSc

facts.value: Some individuals with cancer cachexia have a limited capacity for physical exercise due to various factors.
facts.programme_association: Exercise and Health Fitness Management - BSc

facts.value: Compliance with prescribed exercise is low in individuals with cachexia, and clinical trials often have high drop-out rates.
facts.programme_association: Exercise and Health Fitness Management - BSc

facts.value: There is low-quality evidence for an effect of aerobic physical exercises on anxiety and serious adverse events in adults with hematological malignancies.
facts.programme_association: Exercise and Health Fitness Management - BSc

facts.value: Aerobic physical exercise may result in little to no difference in mortality, quality of life, or physical functioning.

facts.value: Aerobic exercises may result in a slight reduction in depression and fatigue.
